embedded.title: Run rusthinq in Home Assistant

data_description.mqtt_port: Announced to appliances when they register; any free port works

migrate.title: Move an existing rusthinq into Home Assistant
migrate.description:
Keeps the CA your appliances trust, their device records, the LG account and the settings appliances notice, so nothing needs provisioning again.

1. Stop rusthinq on the old host, and keep it stopped: both would answer the same appliances and LG account.
2. In the directory of its config.toml, archive config.toml with the files it names (CA key and certificate, device ledger, LG account and its .pairings), for example:
   `tar czf rusthinq-export.tar.gz config.toml ca.key ca.cert devices.json account.json account.json.pairings`
3. Upload the archive here and choose this host's ports.
4. Point the appliances' route (DNS or redirect) at this host.

data_description.archive: A .tar.gz of config.toml and the files it names
data_description.https_port: Where appliances are provisioned and register (443 unless a redirect points here)
data_description.mqtt_port: Announced to appliances when they register; any free port works

error.invalid_auth: The management API rejected the username or password.
error.invalid_prefix: The topic prefix must not be empty.
error.duplicate_ports: Each listener needs its own port.

ports_unavailable.title: rusthinq cannot open its ports
ports_unavailable.description:
The built-in rusthinq cannot start: {problems}.

Free the port, or choose other ports by removing the integration and adding it again (the CA and devices stay in /config/rusthinq, so nothing is lost). Appliances always open HTTPS on 443; if rusthinq listens elsewhere, redirect 443 to it. rusthinq keeps retrying on its own.

init.title: LG account
init.description:
rusthinq is {state}. Last error: {error}.

The LG account lets rusthinq name your appliances and keep the LG ThinQ app working through its per-device bridge.

menu_options.refresh: Sign in again with the saved credentials

login.title: Sign in to LG
login.description: rusthinq asks LG for a sign-in page for this country.

data_description.country: Two-letter country code of the LG account, e.g. KR or US

login_complete.title: Sign in to LG
login_complete.description:
1. Open [LG's sign-in page]({sign_in_url}) and sign in.
2. The browser ends on a blank page whose address starts with https://…/login/iabClose. Copy that whole address.
3. Paste it here.

logout.title: Sign out of LG
logout.description: rusthinq forgets the LG credentials. Bridged devices disconnect from LG until you sign in again; local control is unaffected.

abort.no_bridge: This rusthinq has no LG bridge.
